title: Every Major AI’s Hidden Advantage Explained in 13 Minutes!
fullText: There are more powerful AI assistants than ever before. Chat, GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grock, Deepseek, Perplexity, Copilot, and the list keeps growing. And if you compare them by benchmarks alone, you'll probably end up more confused than when you started. Because the most important difference between these AIs isn't which one scores a few points higher on a test. It's what each one can do better than almost everyone else. One has an enormous ecosystem behind it. Another can stay on track through massive multi-step projects. One can tap into what's happening online right now, while another can give developers powerful AI for a fraction of the usual cost. So instead of asking which AI is the smartest, let's uncover the hidden advantage that makes each major AI worth using and which one actually makes sense for you. Chat GPT. If you could only pick one AI for everything, chat GPT is usually the answer. Not because it wins every category, but because it covers more categories than anything else. You can write, code, analyze data, generate images, search the web, upload files, do deep research, and connect external apps. All in the same conversation, Claude is often better at long coding tasks. Perplexity is built for search. Gemini has deeper Google integration, but none of them pack this many tools into a single workflow. It also has strong reasoning models for complex multi-step problems. A project's feature that keeps context across sessions and multimodal support for text, images, voice, and files together. That breath comes with a cost, though. Being good at everything sometimes means not being the absolute best at any one thing. If your work is 90% coding or 90% research, a specialized tool might serve you better. But for most people who just need one AI that handles almost anything, Chat GPT is the Swiss Army knife. And that is exactly why it is the default for so many users. Claude. Claude is made by Anthropic. Most people know it for writing well, but that undersells what it actually does. Start with the writing because it is genuinely different. Claude does not just produce text. It produces text that reads like a person wrote it. Tone stays consistent across long documents. Structure holds together even in 3,000word reports. When a prompt has 15 small constraints, this tone, that format, avoid these words, include these points, Claude tends to track all of them without quietly dropping half. That level of instruction following is rare. It also has a feature called skills. You can build a set of custom instructions for a specific type of work, a writing style, a review checklist, a script format, and Claude will follow that skill every time you use it. Instead of pasting the same long prompt over and over, you teach Claude once and reuse it. For anyone who does the same kind of work repeatedly, this saves a lot of time and keeps the output consistent. What really sets Claude apart is how it handles long, complex work. Not a single prompt, a project. Read 200 files, make a plan, edit 25 of them, run tests, find bugs, fix them, and still remember the original goal. Claude Code has become one of Anthropic's standout products for exactly this kind of repository level coding. Where it falls short is breadth. Claude's ecosystem is narrower than chat GBTs, but the things it does, writing that sounds human, skills that keep your workflow locked in, and coding that spans entire repositories, it does them at a level that is hard to match. Gemini Gemini is Google's AI. And to understand its advantage, stop thinking about the model. Think about what sits behind it. Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Calendar, Search, YouTube, Android. Gemini is integrated deeper and deeper into all of them. It does not just answer questions about your work. It sits inside the tools where your work already lives. Another AI can connect to Gmail through an API. Gemini lives inside Gmail. Another AI can search the web. Google owns the search engine. Another AI can read YouTube. Google owns YouTube. Gemini's deep research can pull context from your personal documents, email, and the open web at the same time. On mobile, Gemini has a massive advantage through Android. It could become the default AI layer on billions of phones. But that advantage has a clear boundary. If your company runs on Microsoft 365 or you use Apple everything, the ecosystem benefit shrinks fast. Outside Google apps, Gemini is solid but less differentiated. So, the real question is simple. How deep are you in Google? The deeper you are, the more Gemini makes sense. Grock Grock is made by XAI, and it has access to something no other major AI does. The full fire hose of X, formerly known as Twitter. Most AIs rely on training data that is weeks or months old. Some can search the web, but search engines take time to index new content. Grock searches X directly. It finds posts that went viral 5 minutes ago, tracks reactions to breaking events, and spots trends before they show up on Google. Imagine a CEO posts something controversial 90 seconds ago. A regular AI has no idea. Grock can find that post and show you the reactions in real time. That makes it powerful for breaking news, crypto and stock sentiment, politics, tech launches, and internet culture. Grock has also been improving in coding and agentic tasks. Some versions support context windows up to 2 million tokens, so they can process a huge amount of information at once. Of course, X is not the entire internet. For deep research from academic papers or technical documentation, that advantage does not help much. Grock is strongest when the information you need is fresh, fast, and social. Deepseek. Here is a question most AI comparisons skip. How much should intelligence cost? A model that is 5% better but costs 10 times more is not always the better model especially when you need to process millions of prompts per day. That is where Deepseek changed the conversation. It proved that strong reasoning and coding do not have to come with a premium price tag. Deepseek performs well in math logic and competitive programming. Deepseek v3.2 brought reasoning directly into tool use and was trained for agent environments. And because many DeepSeek models are openweight, developers can download them, run them on their own hardware, and deploy them without depending on someone else's API. Now, the consumer experience is less polished than chat GPT or Claude. The chat interface and ecosystem are thinner. It is also a Chinese company, which raises data handling questions for some users. But for developers and businesses running high volume AI workloads, DeepSeek forced every other lab to answer an uncomfortable question. Why does your model cost this much? Perplexity. Every other AI on this list started as a chatbot and added search later. Perplexity did the opposite. It started from search and built everything around it. That one difference changes the entire experience. Every answer comes with sources by default. You can immediately check where the information came from. That makes perplexity especially strong for factual questions, product comparisons, market research, and anything where you need to verify what the AI is telling you. The old research workflow was search Google, open 10 tabs, read through them, compare, and summarize. Perplexity compresses that into one step. Ask a question with a researched answer with citations, and keep exploring with follow-ups. Its deep research mode can find many sources, cross- reference them, analyze files, and run calculations in a code sandbox. It is not built for long creative writing, complex coding, or multi-step agent work. Perplexity does one thing, but for that one thing, finding reliable sourced answers fast, it is very hard to beat. Microsoft Copilot, ask any regular AI this question. Summarize the Johnson project and tell me what I need to do this week. It has no idea what the Johnson project is. But if the emails, meetings, spreadsheets, and teams discussions for that project live in Microsoft 365, Copilot can pull context from those sources directly. That is its advantage. Not just AI inside Office apps. AI that understands the context of how your company actually works. Microsoft owns Outlook, Teams, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, SharePoint, One Drive, GitHub, and Windows. Copilot sits inside all of them. Microsoft calls this intelligence layer work IQ. It uses context from your email, calendar, meetings, chats, files, and collaboration patterns to understand your work environment. Copilot Co-work can handle longer multi-step tasks instead of just answering single prompts. And the Excel integration alone is a big deal because so much business work still runs on spreadsheets. The catch? C-Pilot's advantage mostly exists inside the Microsoft ecosystem. If your company uses Google Workspace, that enterprise context shrinks significantly. It also requires organizational buyin, not just a personal subscription. Meta AI. Most AI labs are trying to get people to download a new app. Meta skipped that step entirely. WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook, Messenger, that is billions of daily active users. Meta AI is already inside those apps. No new habit, no new download. The AI just shows up where people already spend their time. That distribution advantage is something no other AI company can easily copy. Meta is also pushing into AI glasses through its Ray-B band partnership. That opens a different kind of interface where AI sees the world alongside you instead of living on a phone screen. On the developer side, Meta's Llama models are openweight and used in thousands of products outside Meta. For serious professional work, deep coding, long- form research, complex analysis, other tools are stronger. Meta AI is designed more for casual everyday interactions. But here is the thing most people overlook. The hardest part of building a new AI product is often not the model. It is getting a billion people to use it. Meta already has the billion people. Quen Quen is built by Alibaba and it is one of the most underrated AI ecosystems in the world right now. It is not just one model. It is an entire family. Quen coder for programming, Quenv for vision, Quen Omni for multimodal models of different sizes. So developers can pick a small one for edge devices or a large one for heavy reasoning. And Quen 3 supports 119 languages and dialects, making it one of the strongest multilingual AI systems available. Quen 3 also supports hybrid reasoning. It can switch between a thinking mode for complex problems and a fast mode for simple ones. This lets developers balance speed and intelligence based on what they need. Most Western users have probably never tried Quen directly. Its consumer product is less known outside Asia, but in the developer world, especially for teams building multilingual products or serving Asian markets, Quen is one of the most flexible open model toolkits available. The models are openweight, so you can run them on your own infrastructure and customize them however you want. Mistral vibe. For a regular user, the most important question about AI is which one is smarter? But walk into a bank, a government office or a defense contractor and the questions change completely. Where does our data go? Who owns the infrastructure? Can we run this on our own servers? That is Mistl's territory. Mistl is a French AI company. Mistral Vibe, which evolved from Lashot, offers self-hosting, private cloud deployment, full data residency, fine-tuning for business use cases, and enterprise search across internal documents. It supports over 100 tool connections and has coding agents that work with VS Code and Jet Brains. Mistl is especially relevant to European organizations that want to reduce dependency on American AI providers and to any business in a regulated industry where data control is not optional. On pure benchmarks, Mistl's models are generally not at the top compared to the largest from OpenAI or Google. But for organizations where privacy and control matter more than ranking on a leaderboard, that is a trade-off they are happy to make. Sometimes the best AI is not the smartest one. It is the one you are actually allowed to use. So that is every major AI and its hidden advantage. Chat GPT is the all-rounder. Claude is the long horizon specialist. Gemini has Google behind it. Gro sees the internet in real time. Deepseek makes strong AI cheaper. Perplexity was born for search. Copilot knows your company. Meta AI goes where people already are. Quen gives developers an open multilingual toolkit and Mistl gives enterprises control. The best AI is not the one that wins the most benchmarks. It is the one whose advantage matches what you actually need. Anyway, I also made some other cool videos too. Don't forget to watch them later. Okay.
